memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: She replied, "Do me a special favor. Since you have given me land in the Negev, give me also springs of water." So Caleb gave her the upper and lower springs - Josh 15:19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Achsah has been given land in the Negev — the dry, southern country. Land is good, but land without water in an arid region cannot sustain life. So she asks for something more: springs of water. And her father, generous as ever, gives her not one spring but two — the upper and the lower. He gives more than she asked.

Achsah understood something wise. A gift is not always complete in itself; sometimes we need to ask for what will make the gift truly fruitful. Dry land needs water to flourish. She did not take the land and struggle silently; she came back to her father for the very thing that would bring it to life. And Caleb's abundant answer shows a father who loves to provide fully for his child.

This speaks powerfully to our life with God. He gives us many good things, but He also invites us to come for the living water that alone makes life fruitful. Jesus offered exactly this to a thirsty woman at a well: "Whoever drinks the water I give them will never thirst" (John 4:14). He promised streams of living water — the Spirit — flowing from within those who come to Him (John 7:37-39). Whatever dry ground you are living in, do not settle for land without water. Come to your generous Father and ask for the springs that bring life.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What "dry ground" in your life needs the living water only God can give?
- Are you asking God for what will make His gifts truly fruitful?
- How does Jesus' offer of living water meet your deepest thirst?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are generous beyond my asking. Where my life feels like dry ground, give me the living water of Your Spirit, that I may flourish and not merely survive. Amen.
